title: Johnny Depp Stuns Comic-Con as Ebenezer Scrooge in Major Hollywood Comeback
excerpt: The 63-year-old actor made a surprise appearance at San Diego Comic-Con in full costume and makeup, crashing a panel and debuting the trailer for Ti West's gothic reimagining of A Christmas Carol, set for release on November 13.
body:
• Johnny Depp appeared unannounced at San Diego Comic-Con on Thursday in full Ebenezer Scrooge costume and makeup, his first appearance at the convention since 2018.
  • Depp crashed Collider's "Directors on Directing" panel and delivered an in-character monologue before debuting the trailer for Paramount's Ebenezer: A Christmas Carol.
  • The film, directed by Ti West and co-starring Ian McKellen, Daisy Ridley, and Rupert Grint, opens November 13 and marks Depp's first major studio release since the 2022 Amber Heard defamation trial.
  • Paramount also built an elaborate 1880s British Christmas village activation in San Diego's Gaslamp Quarter, where Depp interacted with fans in character.

A Scrooge Walks Into Comic-Con

https://youtube.com/watch?v=XTQGZ3XL7z4

Johnny Depp pulled off one of the most memorable surprises in San Diego Comic-Con history on Thursday, appearing completely in character as Ebenezer Scrooge at multiple locations across the convention — and leaving fans struggling to recognize the actor beneath layers of Victorian-era makeup and prosthetics.

https://x.com/PeopleOfTheInt/status/2080489907060170811

The 63-year-old actor first turned heads in the Gaslamp Quarter, where Paramount Pictures had constructed an elaborate 1880s British Christmas village activation on Fifth Street. Wearing a top hat, heavy overcoat, and cane, with bushy grey eyebrows and patchy sideburns, Depp puttered around the snowy set in an English accent, tearing garlands off fences and grumbling at performers who tried to spread Christmas cheer, according to Entertainment Weekly.

"Have you all no lives? No responsibility? Why are you here?"

— Johnny Depp, in character as Ebenezer Scrooge at SDCC Hall H

The Hall H Takeover

The real showstopper came inside the convention's legendary Hall H. During Collider's "Directors on Directing" panel — featuring Zach Cregger and the filmmaking duo of Jonathan Goldstein and John Francis Daley discussing their upcoming projects — the lights abruptly cut out. The words "Johnny Depp is Ebenezer" flashed across the screen, and Depp shuffled onto stage carrying a candlestick burned to a stub, USA Today reported.

He delivered a monologue dripping with Scrooge's trademark contempt, asking the crowd why they had bothered to show up before offering to distribute candy — only to scatter it across the stage. As the sounds of rattling chains filled the room and a voice called out Scrooge's name, Depp muttered "Oh, not again. Jacob Marley" and exited to thunderous applause. The first trailer for the film played immediately after.

Outside, Depp was mobbed by cosplayers dressed as his most iconic characters — Captain Jack Sparrow, Edward Scissorhands, Willy Wonka, and the Mad Hatter — creating a visual collision of Depp's career spanning three decades, as reported by Page Six.

Ti West's Gothic Vision

The film, titled Ebenezer: A Christmas Carol, is directed by Ti West, the horror filmmaker behind the critically acclaimed X, Pearl, and MaXXXine trilogy. West's involvement signals a darker, more atmospheric take on the Charles Dickens classic, originally published in 1843.

The cast is stacked. Ian McKellen plays Jacob Marley, Rupert Grint takes on Bob Cratchit, Daisy Ridley plays Emily Cratchit, Andrea Riseborough is the Ghost of Christmas Past, and Tramell Tillman portrays the Ghost of Christmas Present. Sam Claflin, Arthur Conti, and Ellie Bamber round out the ensemble. Production began in January 2026 in Dublin and London, according to Just Jared.

The trailer leans heavily into meta territory. Opening text reads: "He brought us Jack Sparrow, Edward Scissorhands and the Mad Hatter. This Thanksgiving, the master of misfits returns." The official logline keeps it punchy: "The name you know, the story you don't."

Depp's Return to the Mainstream

Ebenezer marks a significant career milestone for Depp, whose Hollywood trajectory was upended by his acrimonious legal battle with ex-wife Amber Heard. The defamation trial concluded in June 2022, with a jury finding that Heard had defamed Depp in a 2018 Washington Post op-ed. The case was later settled after Heard appealed the verdict.

This will be Depp's first major wide release by an American studio since 2018's Fantastic Beasts: The Crimes of Grindelwald, and his first Comic-Con appearance in eight years. In the interim, Depp directed and starred in the independent French film Modì and kept a lower profile in Hollywood.

Depp even wove in a sly political jab during his Gaslamp appearance. When a performer placed decorations on a fence near him, Depp stayed in character: "That's on my property, which means that I own it. And you're paying tax on it being there. 'Cause everybody has to pay all that stuff. Putting tariffs on the gate" — a quip that drew knowing laughs from the crowd, Entertainment Weekly reported.

What's Next

Paramount has set Ebenezer: A Christmas Carol for a November 13 theatrical release, positioning it as a Thanksgiving-season tentpole. For fans of Depp's chameleon-like approach to characters — from Sparrow's drunken swagger to Scissorhands' silent vulnerability — Scrooge represents exactly the kind of eccentric, costume-heavy role that made him a global star. Whether Depp can translate Thursday's Comic-Con buzz into a genuine box-office comeback remains the biggest question heading into awards season.
nri_angle: Johnny Depp's massive global fanbase includes millions in India and across the diaspora, where his Pirates of the Caribbean and Charlie and the Chocolate Factory franchises are cultural touchstones. The star-studded cast featuring Harry Potter's Rupert Grint, Star Wars' Daisy Ridley, and Lord of the Rings' Ian McKellen spans fandoms with deep resonance in Indian pop culture.
